title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes develop an order-theoretic axiomatics. An 'atelier' satisfies axioms At 1–At 7, and an 'atlas' adds axioms on 'lieux' (AtL1–AtL3, AtCL(spec)). The data are a set M with two order relations, ≤ (a 'sub-locus' relation) and ≪ (a stronger, 'relatively compact / lies well inside' kind of relation), together with a compatibility relation ≭. L is the set of ≤-minimal elements (the 'points'), and ∥ is a given symmetric irreflexive 'disjunction' relation on L. For X in M, omb(X) (the 'ombre', or shadow) is the set of points x with x ≪ X, and omb(X)° is its 'interior' part, the points with x ∘≪ X. Here ∘≪ is a strengthened form of ≪.

On pp. 30–31 Grothendieck builds, from (M, ≤, ≪, ∥), a compatibility relation ≭_M on M. He checks that the resulting structure is an atelier whose family F consists of the closed subsets of M made of pairwise compatible elements. Only At_M 4 remains to be checked.

This page reduces that remaining point to Lemma 6: if Z ∘≪ X, Z ∘≪ Y and X ≭ Y, then X = Y. Two compatible elements that both contain a common element 'in their interior' coincide, a separation or uniqueness property.

Lemma 6 follows from a Corollary: if X ≭ Y, Z ∘≪ X and Z ≪ Y, then X ≤ Y.
- Proof: by ML 2, omb(Z)° is nonempty; pick x in it.
- Then x ∘≪ Z ∘≪ X, so x ∘≪ X by transitivity (lemma 2, cor. 4, p. 29). Hence x ∈ omb(X)°.
- Also x ∈ omb(Y), implicitly via x ≪ Z ≪ Y.
- So omb(X)° ∩ omb(Y) ≠ ∅, and Lemma 4 (compatible plus 'interior shadow meets shadow' implies ≤) gives X ≤ Y.
- Exchanging X and Y and using antisymmetry gives Lemma 6.

Lemma 7 checks that the original ∥ on L is recovered as the disjunction relation of the constructed atelier:
- (a) For x, y ∈ L: x ≭ y iff x = y or x ∥ y.
- (b) x ∥ y iff x ≭ y and Inf^≤(x, y) = ∅, i.e. x and y are disjoint in the atelier sense.
- Proof of (a), case x ≠ y: x and y are minimal, so omb(x) = {x}, omb(y) = {y}. The common-lower-bound set L = x̃ ∩ ỹ (notation of p. 31) is empty. The defining condition for compatibility (p. 31) then reduces exactly to x ∥ y. Part (b) follows.

This feeds Lemma 8 and the 'Théorème-Scholie' on p. 33. That theorem characterizes intrinsically which (M, ≤, ≪, ∥) arise from an atlas satisfying At1–At7, AtL1–AtL3 and AtCL(spec). In effect it is a reconstruction or representation theorem for the combinatorial 'tame-topology' structures of Analysis situs.
errors: In the Corollary's proof, x ∈ omb(Y) is asserted without comment; it requires x ≪ Z (from x ∘≪ Z) and transitivity of ≪ with Z ≪ Y. This is a harmless gap.
Deducing Lemma 6 from the Corollary tacitly uses symmetry of ≭ and antisymmetry of ≤. This is fine but unstated.
The proof of Lemma 7 is very terse; 'L = ∅' must be read as x̃ ∩ ỹ = ∅ for distinct minimal elements, and the proof of (b) is cut off at the page end.

ideas.what: Separation lemma: compatible elements sharing a common element in their 'interior' (∘≪) are equal; more generally ≤-comparable.
ideas.modern_name: uniqueness/separation property in an abstract 'atlas' of charts (analogous to Hausdorff-type uniqueness of maximal charts, or interpolation/way-below arguments in continuous posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: no specific attribution; part of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatics

ideas.what: Recovering the given disjunction relation ∥ on minimal elements as the intrinsic disjointness (compatible and no common lower bound) of the reconstructed atelier.
ideas.modern_name: consistency/representation step in an order-theoretic reconstruction theorem (cf. incompatibility relations in Boolean or forcing posets, disjointness in frames)

ideas.what: Overall program: axiomatize 'lieux' via a set with two orders (≤, ≪), shadows omb(X), interior shadows omb(X)°, and a compatibility/disjunction relation, then characterize which such data come from atlases (Théorème-Scholie, p. 33).
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial/point-free approach to tame topology; akin to proximity/de Vries structures and continuous posets with a way-below relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) announces tame topology; the point-free analogues are due to de Vries (1962), Scott and Gierz et al. (1970s–80)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme sketches 'topologie modérée' only programmatically; the atelier/atlas axiomatics itself appears unpublished

missed.claim: The atelier/atlas framework (two order relations ≤ and ≪, an 'interior' version ∘≪, shadows, and a compatibility/disjunction relation, with a reconstruction theorem) parallels point-free topology structures. These include de Vries compingent relations and continuous posets with the way-below relation. The Analysis situs notes seem not to have been compared with these in the literature.
missed.quote: Cor. On a, si X ≭ Y : Z ∘≪ X, Z ≪ Y ⇒ X ≤ Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Making the dictionary explicit could place Grothendieck's tame-topology axiomatics within locale and domain theory, or show where it genuinely differs, for example through the compatibility relation tailored to gluing charts.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine verification step (Lemmas 6–7) inside an unpublished axiomatic construction. The surrounding framework is of historical interest as unpublished material, but nothing on this page itself is a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'amb(Z)°', 'amb(X)°', 'amb(Y)' should be 'omb(Z)°', 'omb(X)°', 'omb(Y)' (ombre), consistent with p. 31; likewise the marginal note reads 'omb x = {x}, omb(y) = {y}'.
'covariation minimale' is likely a misreading; probably 'caractère minimal' or similar (referring to minimality of x, y in L).
The first line is 'correspondant : un atelier At 1 – At 7.' after a struck-out word.
'L'énoncé b) résulte[?]' reads plausibly as 'L'énoncé b) résulte,' with the sentence continuing off-page.
